displayPattern: Dishwasher display shows 999 (it may also flash). The dishwasher will not start or run.
meaning: Control reset needed, or a possible leak: on most models 999 means the control needs to be reset, but on models with the Floor Protect with Alert feature GE says it indicates a possible leak.
causes: The control needs a reset (GE lists GDT225SGLBB, GDT225SGLWW, GDT225SSLSS, PDT145SGLBB, PDT145SGLWW, PDT145SSLSS, ZDT165SILII and ZDT165SSLSS for this)
On models with Floor Protect with Alert: moisture in the pan under the dishwasher, which GE treats as a possible leak
diySteps: Check your model: if your dishwasher has Floor Protect with Alert, treat 999 as a possible leak. GE says the dishwasher will not start and to contact service; do not keep resetting it
On the other models, press and hold the Cycle Select and Start pads together for 5 seconds, or until 999 goes away. A blank display or another number is acceptable
Press any button to finish the reset. 130 or another cycle time may appear in the display, and the dishwasher is then ready to use
If the dishwasher is also beeping while showing a leak message, GE says to disconnect power to it until it can be repaired
safetyNote: Switch the dishwasher off at its breaker before you reach into the base or remove a filter or cover, and let the tub and water cool after a cycle. Watch for sharp debris. Pump, heater, valve and control-board repairs belong to a qualified appliance technician. If water is on the floor, switch off the breaker before you step in it or mop near the dishwasher.
proAdvice: Call for service if your model has Floor Protect with Alert, if there is water under the dishwasher, or if 999 returns after the Cycle Select + Start reset. GE says leaking from underneath the dishwasher always needs service.
